title: Electrons are immortal: no beta decay for elementary trefoils
html:
Beta decay rearranges the crossing orientation partition of the Borromean baryon (e.g., [u,d,d] \to [u,u,d]). It relies on internal composite structure rearranged via R-I moves.

Stability of the electron against beta decay

The electron avoids beta decay through topological necessity. The electron braid \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3 (closing to the positive Hopf link T(2,2); single-component alternative T_{2,3}) possesses no internal quark-flavour partition to rearrange via mixed crossings. Its single degree of freedom is its global topological invariant.

Particle Structure Internal d.o.f. Beta decay?
Neutron [u,d,d]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H Quark flavour partition Yes: \mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \nu^{\sigma}
Proton [u,u,d]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H Quark flavour partition Yes (in nuclei): \mathfrak{p} \to \mathfrak{n} + e^+ + \nu
Electron \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \to T(2,2) (alt. T_{2,3}) None No
Neutrino T_{1,0} (unknot) None No

No lighter charged lepton exists. The neutrino T_{1,0} cannot absorb the electron's topological charge.

Electron survival to heat death

The time reversal barrier prevents chirality reversal during the observable era (1 < q < \infty). The electron persists immortally from pair production to the cosmological boundary.

As the universe approaches heat death (q \to 1):

  1. Bound electrons are liberated: Binding energy dissipates while bare mass remains invariant.
  2. Free electrons become radiation: The crossing energy asymmetry q - q^{-1} \to 0 erases Coulomb charge. The electron becomes a massless topological excitation.
  3. Radiation becomes CMB: The thermal photon bath redshifts to the CMB. The CMB torsion signature records the q-deformed Reeb flow.

Into the next aeon

If the cosmological chirality flip holds, CMB radiation carries topological data across the heat-death boundary. Frobenius degeneration governs this aeon transition. Exceptional divisors reset the topology. The electron braid closure persists to the q = 1 boundary.
